newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares ease, dealers look to future.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares ease, dealers look to future.

text.p: * The official index fell 0.04 points to 908.80
* The group A index eased 36.75 points to 1,982.19.
* Central market turnover was a sluggish 535,000 litas.
Lithuania's bourse remained in a bearish mood on Thursday but dealers said they had hopes for the future.

Dealers said that a two-day conference which began Thursday on the country's capital markets was a useful marketing tool and was generating foreign interest in the bourse, which has been struggling through a painful correction in recent months.
But they said that the results would not be immediate.
"The conference is a very serious move but its impact on the market might not be felt until later in the year," one dealer said.
Sluggish turnover of 535,000 litas on the central market and 192,000 litas in block trades left little room for optimism in the near future.
Spirits producer Sema fell 9.92 percent to 6.45 litas on turnover of 61,000 litas.
"When the government, which holds a big stake in the company, acts indecisively, it always irritates the investors and pushes the price down," one dealer said.
The government holds a 27 percent stake in the company and it is still remains unclear whether it will use its priority right to buy into Sema's new 18 million litas share issue.
The Lithuanian Sea Shipping (LISCO) company inched up to 6.48 litas from 6.40 litas on turnover of 57,000 litas.
"The prices of LISCO were very low and they had to go up," one dealer said.
The banking sector remained cool with the exception of Siauliu Bank, which advanced to 90.00 litas from 86.00 litas in trade of 45,000 litas on the central market.
